title: 电源与 GND：电流回家的路
summary: 一个 LED 明明接上了电却不亮——因为电流找不到回家的路。
description: 电流从电源 + 出发，必须回到电源 −。电源 − 那一端通常定为 GND（0 V 参考点）。本课先搭一条没有回路的支路，再给它接上回家的路，最后让两条支路共用同一个 GND。

cards.title: LED 接上了，为什么不亮？
text: 先搭半条支路：电池、跳线、电阻、LED 都插好了，**唯独少一根线**。
搭完看 LED：它亮不亮？再看右边**诊断**怎么说。

cards.title: 电流要回家
text: - 电流从电池 **+** 出发，穿过元件，**必须回到电池 −**。只出不回，就一点电流都没有——LED 的短脚悬在空中，圈没有闭合。
- **电压是两点之间的差。** 说“这里是 9 V”，其实省略了“相对谁”。这个默认的参考点叫 **GND**（地），规定它是 **0 V**。
- 我们把电池的 **− 端定为 GND**：红轨 = VCC（+9 V），蓝轨 = GND（0 V）。
- GND 不是大地，也不是“电流消失的地方”。电流到了 GND 还要继续流，回到电池里。

cards.title: 给它一条回家的路
text: 补上回路，再照样搭第二条支路。两条支路的“家”是**同一条蓝轨**。

cards.title: 带走
text: - 原理图上的接地符号 ⏚ 意思是“接到电源 −”。图上画了五个 ⏚，实物里它们全是**同一个结点**。
- **LED 不亮，先找回路**：从它的短脚出发，看能不能一路走回电池 −。
- 习惯：**红线接 +，黑线或蓝线接 −**。真实电路里这能救命——接反电源是烧板子最常见的原因。
下一个：LED 为什么一定要串电阻。

en.title: Power and GND: the way home
en.summary: An LED is connected to power and still stays dark — because the current can't find its way home.
en.description: Current leaves the supply at + and has to get back to −. The supply's − terminal is usually called GND, the 0 V reference. In this lesson you first build a branch with no way back, then give it one, and finally let two branches share the same GND.
hints: You don't need to run each branch back to the battery on the red rail: the whole rail is already connected.
An LED stays dark? First check that its short lead has a path to the blue rail.
tests: Both LEDs on, VCC and GND at the right voltages

cards.title: It's connected — so why is it dark?
text: First build half a branch: battery, jumper, resistor and LED are all in place, **except for one wire**.
Then look at the LED: is it lit? And what do the **diagnostics** on the right say?

cards.title: Current has to get home
text: - Current leaves the battery at **+**, goes through the parts and **must get back to the battery −**. Out without a way back means no current at all — the LED's short lead is hanging in the air, so the loop is open.
- **A voltage is a difference between two points.** "This point is at 9 V" leaves out "relative to what". That default reference point is called **GND** (ground) and it is **0 V** by definition.
- We make the battery's **− terminal GND**: red rail = VCC (+9 V), blue rail = GND (0 V).
- GND is not the earth, and it is not "where current disappears". At GND the current keeps flowing, back into the battery.

cards.title: Give it a way home
text: Close the loop, then build a second branch the same way. Both branches go home to **the same blue rail**.

cards.title: Take away
text: - The ground symbol ⏚ on a schematic means "connected to the supply −". Five ⏚ symbols on a drawing are **one single node** in the real circuit.
- **LED dark? Look for the loop first**: start at its short lead and check that you can walk all the way back to the battery −.
- Habit: **red wires for +, black or blue for −**. In real circuits this saves boards — a reversed supply is the most common way to fry one.
Next: why an LED always needs a resistor.

steps: Pick **Battery**: red lead (+) in **`tp1`**, black lead (−) in **`tn1`**. From now on the whole red rail is +9 V and the whole blue rail is GND.
**Resistor R1** (set **`470 Ω`** in Properties) in **`c5`**–**`c8`**; **red LED1** long lead in **`d8`**, short lead in **`d10`**. Is LED1 lit?
Blue **jumper**: **`a10`** → **`tn10`**. LED1's short lead now has a way back to GND — is it lit now?
A second branch, further right: red jumper **`tp15`** → **`a15`**; **R2** (**`470 Ω`**) in **`c15`**–**`c18`**; **yellow LED2** long lead **`d18`**, short lead **`d20`**.
Blue **jumper** **`a20`** → **`tn20`**. Both LEDs are lit, and both go home to **the same blue rail**. Press **Check my circuit**.

measurements.ask: The schematic draws a ground symbol ⏚ under LED1 and another under LED2. On the breadboard they are:
choices: One node: both short leads go through jumpers to the same blue rail
Two different nodes that just look the same on paper
measurements.explain: Every ground symbol means "connected to the supply −". They are one point in the real circuit, which is why it is called one GND node.

measurements.ask: What happens if you pull out the blue jumper a10 → tn10?
choices: Only LED1 goes out; LED2 stays lit
measurements.explain: LED2 has its own way home (a20 → tn20). Every branch needs its own path to GND.

tests.name: 两个 LED 都亮，VCC 和 GND 的电压正确

measurements.ask: 原理图上 LED1 和 LED2 下面各画了一个接地符号 ⏚。在面包板上，它们是：
choices: 同一个结点：两个短脚都通过跳线接到同一条蓝轨
两个不同的结点，只是画法一样
measurements.explain: 所有接地符号都表示“接到电源 −”。它们在实物里是同一个点，所以叫同一个 GND 结点。

measurements.ask: 如果拔掉 a10 → tn10 那根蓝跳线，会怎样？
choices: 只有 LED1 灭，LED2 照样亮
measurements.explain: LED2 有自己的回路（a20 → tn20），不受影响。每条支路都要有自己通往 GND 的路。

steps.text: 选**「电池」**：**`tp1`** 放红线（+），**`tn1`** 放黑线（−）。从现在起，整条红轨是 +9 V，整条蓝轨是 GND。
蓝色**跳线**：**`a10`** → **`tn10`**。LED1 的短脚有路回到 GND 了——它亮了吗？
蓝色**跳线** **`a20`** → **`tn20`**。两个 LED 都亮了，而且它们回到的是**同一条蓝轨**。点**「检查我的电路」**。

hints: 红轨不需要每条支路都连回电池：整条轨道本来就是通的。
某个 LED 不亮？先检查它的短脚有没有一条路通到蓝轨。
